written_from: IBM z/OS 3.1.0 MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385): EXEC COND parameter, IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF statement construct. Expected answers were written before any evaluator existed.
scenario_input: given: per step that starts, {rc: n} (0-4095) or {abend: code}. A step with no entry in given does not start.
scenario_answer: expect: per step, run (started, whether it ended with an RC or abended) or bypass (did not start).

scenarios.basis: S2 (4,LT,S1): 4 < 0 false. S3: 8 <= 0 false, 0 NE 0 false. S4 (4,GT) tests every earlier step: 4 > 0 true, bypass. S5 EVEN: no abend, no test coded, runs. S6 ONLY: nothing abended, bypass.
S2: 4 < 6 true, bypass. S3: 8 <= 6 false; the test on bypassed S2 is false (IBM: a previously bypassed step evaluates false), runs. S4: 4 > 6 false but 4 > 0 (S3) true, bypass.
S2: 4 < 8 true. S3: 8 <= 8 true. S4: 4 > 8 false, tests on bypassed S2 and S3 false, runs.

After an abend the system bypasses the following steps (S2, S3, S4 carry no EVEN / ONLY). EVEN does not test an abended step and no other test is coded, so S5 runs; ONLY runs because a preceding step abended.
As cond-s1-abend, the abend comes later; S1 and S2 had run normally.
T2: no abend, (4,LT,T1) 4 < 0 false, EVEN runs it. T3: ONLY and nothing abended, bypass.
T2: EVEN indicates run, then the test 4 < 8 is satisfied, bypass (IBM: EVEN / ONLY first, then the tests). T3: nothing abended, bypass.
EVEN and ONLY do not test the RC of an abended step, so no test is satisfied: T2 runs (EVEN), T3 runs (a preceding step abended).
I1.RC = 0 true: THEN. RC = 0 and I2.RC = 0: second IF false. ABEND false. I3 did not start, so I3.RUN = FALSE is true (ASSUMED, see assumed).
I1.RC = 0 false: ELSE. RC is 4, not > 4; I2 did not execute, so I2.RC = 4 is false. I3 started, so I3.RUN = FALSE is false.
RC = 4 is not > 4, but I2.RC = 4 is true, so I4 runs. I3.RUN = FALSE true (ASSUMED).
ELSE ran I3 with RC 0; RC stays the highest so far, 12 > 4 true, I4 runs.

An abended step is not evaluated for RC, so I1.RC = 0 is false (ELSE), but after an abend the system bypasses following steps unless the IF names ABEND, ABENDCC or the negated ABEND: only I5's IF does. INFERRED from that sentence, see assumed.
As if-i1-abend: I4's and I6's IFs do not name ABEND, so IF RC > 4 cannot rescue I4; I5 runs.

datasets: CONDJOB S1 creates APP.LEVEL.WORK (NEW, CATLG, DELETE) and S2 reads it. IBM: a dataset a bypassed or abended step was to create 'may not exist, may not be cataloged, or may be incomplete'. Undefined by IBM, so no scenario compares a dataset: the shape test checks only the DD bindings the reader reports.

assumed.text: A step that never started for a reason other than its own COND (not run because of an IF clause, after an abend) is a bypassed step for a later COND test: false. IBM states the rule for a bypassed step only.

stepname.RUN = FALSE on a step that did not start evaluates true. IBM's relationexp page says a relational expression naming a step that did not execute is false; the RUN page says the test is for a step that did not start. Settled for RUN as documented, false for stepname.RC / ABEND / ABENDCC.

After an ordinary abend an IF whose expression does not name ABEND, ABENDCC or the negated ABEND does not start its step. Inferred from the sentence on the COND page; the IF pages say it only for cancel, time expiry and scheduling abends (the clause is skipped regardless of the tests).

EVEN / ONLY Table 2 (Effect of EVEN and ONLY on Step Execution): the cell alignment was lost in extraction. The rows here follow IBM's prose (EVEN does not test abended steps; ONLY runs only after an abend; EVEN / ONLY first, then the tests). Re-read the live table before pinning its rows.
